endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Establish/modify a vendor security assessment process. Create a standardized questionnaire that all AI vendors must complete before contracting.

endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: ix) Da ta Use Policy: (1) Privacy.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI
endorsements.quote: Require third-party vendors to comply with all data security and privacy requirements outlined in the agreement, including encryption, access controls, and regular security assessments.

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The team should also determine whether the implementer team’s organization has policies and procedures that require third-party suppliers to meet specific privacy and cybersecurity objectives.

endorsements.title: Choosing the right artificial intelligence solutions for your radiology department: key factors to consider
endorsements.quote: Data security measures: Evaluate the AI system\u2019s data security measures, including encryption protocols and access controls, to ensure patient data are protected, particularly if cloud-based solutions are used.

endorsements.title: The Elastic Electronic Health Record: A Five-Tiered Framework for Applying Artificial Intelligence to Electronic Health Record Maintenance, Configuration, and Use
endorsements.quote: Ensure all data in transit or at rest is encrypted.

commentary.bottom_line: Six sources endorse vendor security questionnaires, independent certification, and contractual security commitments, but no study supplied here tests whether these requirements reduce breaches of patient data or systems. The recommendation currently rests on expert consensus and analogy to general information-security practice rather than on outcome data from health care AI deployments.

perspectives.view: No study tests the practice, and no study documents the hazard in AI vendor settings. The six endorsements include two frameworks, two guidance documents, and two commentaries, and only the CHAI playbook states the requirement as a must. Consistent agreement among sources reflects consensus, which GRADE does not treat as evidence of effect.

The supplied record contains no data on how often AI vendors cause breaches, which failure points questionnaires or certification would catch, or how much harm follows. Without hazard or outcome studies, the size of the risk this safeguard addresses and the share of it the safeguard removes both remain unmeasured.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare breach incidents, security findings, or time to remediation between health systems that require vendor questionnaires, independent certification, and contractual testing rights and those that do not. Research should also measure how often AI vendors fail these assessments and whether contract terms such as testing rights are exercised in practice.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may have less staff capacity to run vendor assessments and enforce contract terms, and the absence of data leaves the feasibility and effect of this requirement in those settings unknown.
